description: Ainexa Team is a multidisciplinary team from Uzbekistan focused on AI, cybersecurity, software development and space technology. We build practical solutions using NASA open data and innovative technologies.
summary: Ember Atlas unifies 25 years of NASA's MODIS and VIIRS active-fire records into one consistent fire record, and turns it into a burning-activity calendar for any area on Earth. The two sensors measure fire differently: VIIRS (375 m, since 2012) detects about four times more fires than MODIS (1 km, since 2000), so the raw record shows a fake jump in 2012. We calibrated MODIS to VIIRS for every 5° region and season, using the years both satellites flew. On years the method never saw (2019–2025), the monthly error fell from 76% to 7.4%. On this single record, anyone can pick a country, province or drawn box and see when it burns: the critical period, a "get ready by" month, and which months were unusual compared with 25 years of normal. Live mode merges four satellites so each fire is counted once and filters out gas flares, volcanoes and industry. An AI forecast, trained on the unified record plus NASA POWER weather, vegetation and forest data, gives fire risk for this month and next with an explanation. On unusual fires it is 73% more precise than "same as usual". It is free, open and runs in any browser.
details:
What it does Ember Atlas answers a question the raw satellite record cannot: *"When does my area burn, and is this year unusual?"* NASA has detected active fires from space for 25 years, but with two different instruments. MODIS (Terra/Aqua, 1 km pixels, since 2000) and VIIRS (375 m pixels, since 2012) see different numbers of fires: VIIRS reports about 4× more because it sees smaller fires. Joined as they are, the records show global fire quadrupling in 2012, which never happened. Ember Atlas harmonizes them into one VIIRS-equivalent record and builds four tools on it:

-- History: 392.6 million detections (Nov 2000 – Dec 2025) on a 0.5° monthly grid on a 3D globe; a Raw switch shows the 2012 artefact disappear.

-- Fire Calendar: pick a country, province/republic or draw a box to get a year × month burning-activity calendar. It shows the critical period (fewest months holding 80% of a normal year's fire), a "get ready by" month, unusual months (≥2 robust spreads from that calendar month's median, log scale), a Theil–Sen trend with a Mann–Kendall test, CSV download and a shareable link.

-- Live: NASA FIRMS near-real-time data from VIIRS (NOAA-20, NOAA-21) and MODIS (Terra, Aqua). The same fire seen by several satellites is counted once. Gas flares, volcanoes and industrial heat can be filtered out using a mask built from 25 years of FIRMS labels, VIIRS Nightfire and the Smithsonian volcano list. Clicking a fire shows NASA GIBS and Sentinel-2 imagery of it.

-- AI Forecast: the chance of significant fire per 1° square for this month and next, with an explanation (fire history, current weather anomalies, past years with similar weather). For any chosen area it shows whether risk is higher or lower than usual and ranks the provinces.
